top_local_reviews.title: Huge help for nighttime congestion
top_local_reviews.review_text: I originally picked this up because I kept getting stuffy at night whenever I laid down. Still not sure if it’s allergies from pollen, my cats, or both, but this has helped a ton with opening up my nasal passages and making it easier to breathe while trying to sleep. What I like most is that it gives real relief without going down the slippery slope of constantly using something like Afrin. It works well without that harsh rebound effect you hear about from overusing nasal decongestant sprays. The Kirkland version has honestly been just as effective for me as the big name brands at a way better price, especially considering how many bottles you get in the pack. If you deal with nighttime congestion or seasonal allergies, this is absolutely worth keeping on hand.

top_local_reviews.review_text: That's much more specific and believable. I'd write it something like this: I've dealt with a stuffy nose for years thanks to Central Texas allergies, and for the longest time I relied on the usual decongestant nasal sprays for relief. I knew Flonase existed, but never wanted to spend the money, and somehow it never occurred to me to look for a generic version. Then a coworker brought me a bottle of Kirkland Aller-Flo to try, and it was honestly life changing! When that bottle finally ran out, I went looking for more online instead of asking her to make another Costco run for me. I was thrilled to find this 5-pack on Amazon for not much more than Costco's price. This spray has made a huge difference for me. It doesn't burn my nostrils the way some sprays do, and I don't experience the rebound effects I got from the decongestant sprays I used before. I also don't find myself needing to use more and more over time to get the same relief. If allergies keep your nose stuffed up year-round, this has definitely been worth it for me.

top_local_reviews.title: Gentle, Effective, and Reliable Relief at a Great Value
top_local_reviews.review_text: Gentle, Effective, and Reliable Relief at a Great Value Kirkland Signature’s Stool Softener has become my dependable choice for maintaining regularity without harsh side effects. Each softgel contains 100 mg of docusate sodium — the same active ingredient as Colace — but at a fraction of the cost. The 400-count bottle is an excellent value and lasts for months, even with daily use. What I like most is how gentle this formula is. It doesn’t cause cramping or urgency — just a smooth, predictable result when taken consistently with adequate hydration. The softgels are small, easy to swallow, and completely tasteless. I’ve found it works especially well post-surgery or when taking medications that can cause constipation. The product quality is consistent, and I’ve never noticed any melting or capsule sticking, even during warm months. Kirkland’s formulation feels clean and reliable — you know exactly what you’re getting. Bottom line: Kirkland’s Stool Softener provides the same dependable relief as Colace at a fraction of the price. Gentle, effective, and budget-friendly — it’s a must-have staple in any home medicine cabinet.

top_local_reviews.subtitle: Reviewed in the United States on February 14, 2022
top_local_reviews.title: Helped After My Appendectomy
top_local_reviews.review_text: I’ve always had an issue with having regular bowel movements so in order not to be constipated (cuz let’s be real, constipation can be very painful) I try to take these stool softener on a daily basis. Sometimes I forget to take them but normally I’m pretty good about it. Last year, on a cold November night I was awoken with pain in my abdomen. It was the kind of pain that makes you take notice and doesn’t let you fall asleep. At first I thought it could be cramps or even constipation but even after taking a laxative (not a stool softener) this pain would not go away. I briefly considered it might be my appendix but since I didn’t have chills, fever or nausea I dismissed that idea from my brain. I wish I didn’t because 24 hrs later I ended up in the emergency room having surgery on an “acute” perforated appendix. While at the hospital they loaded me up on antibiotics and pain medication which ironically caused me to be constipated. Now for anyone whose had surgery, you know that to have a bowel movement will now be very painful. I’m glad the doctors and nurses recommended that I take a stool softener because with all the meds I was taking and all the pain I was in I might have forgotten to take it. After having my appendix removed at old age of 52 and suffering  a subsequent wound infection because of my appendix I am now religiously taking at least 2 of these a day. After the surgery I did purchase the Colace at CVS because my doctor recommended it but I’ve since gone back to using these and have not noticed a change in effectiveness. I have however noticed a change in my wallet. Lol. PS.  Moral of the story is this…. If you have pain in your abdomen for more than 8 hours then take yourself to the hospital. Don’t wait for almost 24 hours like I did. If I had waited longer I might not be alive to write this review. Also if your bowel movements are irregular, it wouldn’t hurt to pop one of these pills daily to help in that area. I know it has helped me. 😍😍😍

top_local_reviews.subtitle: Reviewed in the United States on July 16, 2018
top_local_reviews.title: Finally relief from a loud neighborhood and snoring BF!
top_local_reviews.review_text: My boyfriend and I recently moved to an apartment in the middle of a bar/night club district in Downtown Cleveland. It's very, very loud on the weekends, and surprisingly, some weekdays as well. I have now discovered that my boyfriend will sleep through practically anything and also is a chronic loud snorer. Having trouble adjusting from a quiet, dead end suburban street and a bed to myself to a bustling metropolitan area with obnoxious drunks yelling, motorcycles throttling, the occasional food truck running 30 feet below our window, and a boyfriend who sounds like he is revving up a chainsaw in his sleep, I decided that I needed to experiment with products that would help me fall asleep and stay asleep. Earplugs felt uncomfortable in my ears and didn't mask all the noise. A white noise app just made it sound like my boyfriend was snoring through the middle of a fake thunderstorm. A fan made the room too cold and wasn't loud enough anyway. Melatonin didn't phase me one bit. Benadryl gave me a groggy hangover the whole next day. ZzzQuil made me have nightmares - like, terrifying, wake up yelling and sweating nightmares. So I started researching different active ingredients in sleep aids and reading reviews on both Amazon and Reddit. This one was decently priced, contained ingredients different than what I had already tried, and was rated highly. It is the generic form of Unisom. The first few days using this, I indeed woke up a couple times in the middle of the night and felt groggy the next morning. I decided to split the pill in half and take a half dose about 1-2 hours before bedtime. It now works perfectly for me - by the time I'm headed to bed I can barely keep my eyes open and I'm only waking up once or twice and falling back asleep pretty easily. I used to wake up 5-6 times a night, sometimes up to every half hour, and have trouble falling back asleep. This supplement has made me sleep sounder and, in turn, I feel better overall during the day. I used to come home from work and take a nap at 5 PM because I was so tired, but now I feel awake, my skin has cleared up, it's easier to lose weight, and I don't feel as stressed out. It even knocked me out for half of an 11-hour drive to the Outer Banks, something I've never been able to sleep through before. The only downsides of this medication are that sometimes when I don't take it (traveling, a late night out, forgetfulness) I find it difficult to fall asleep, but I don't think it's bad/often enough that it's habit-forming. Another downside is that I do not know the long-term effects of taking an antihistamine sleeping pill. Everyone will react differently to different medications - if you're trying this one, perhaps start with half a dose and understand that you may feel groggy while your body gets "used to it". For reference - I am a 125 lb female, which is perhaps why the full dose was too strong for me.

top_local_reviews.subtitle: Reviewed in the United States on October 28, 2015
top_local_reviews.title: A relief and a gateway to sleepyness, please read my comment.
top_local_reviews.review_text: I have terrible insomnia and use a Benzo drug called Serax, to sleep. I don't like using it too often because Benzo's are addictive. A friend of mine suggested this sleep aid, because it's basically Unisom under the Kirkland drug store name.  It's non addictive and it's also an antihistamine. So if you have allergies it may be helpful, but it does make you sleepy. Sometimes I can just take half and it makes me sleepy but then sometimes I need two pills to actually make me sleep.  I don't use them daily, only about one or twice a week.  The one thing I don't like about these are they make me groggy the next day, and it takes almost the full day to shake that off. I try to use them only on weekends so it doesn't interfere with my weekly schedule for work and outings. It didn't make me sleepy within and hour, it took awhile. I take it at 9 pm and I'm only asleep at 11:30-midnight. So I think it depends on the person for ability to make you fall asleep, each time I use it seems a little different. If I use it many days in a row, it seems like it stops working, but that could be because of my type of insomnia.  If you get used to a drug and have to take more every few months, this may happen to you as well. Sometimes it gives me a headache the following day, I never get headaches normally.  It's a good product when you're having a bout of insomnia. Sometimes I also have hives or itching hands from anxiety and stress, and the antihistamine properties really helps me with that, I need only about 1/4 of the pill when I get hives or itchiness. I think it's a very helpful medication, definitely worth a try. Insomnia can make us desperate, and I've tried taking medications, working out to wear myself out, and even alcohol shots before bed, nothing really worked, but most times this helps me feel sleepy. I never feel sleepy and if you're like me, you know how wonderful it can feel when suddenly you feel sleepy.  It also makes me dream more than usual, I've never had bad dreams with this, only funny and strangely adventurous dreams, but it makes taking this pill even more worth it, I enjoy dreaming and journaling them afterwards. Worth a try in my opinion. Way cheaper than prescription medication, and no risk for addiction.

top_local_reviews.subtitle: Reviewed in the United States on February 5, 2024
top_local_reviews.title: SAVES MONEY: 1 Roll last nearly a YEAR
top_local_reviews.review_text: (Scroll all the way day for an easy way to reheat rice back to the fresh made state.) You WILL save money and frustration using better wrap. My sister once told me that this is “so expense” and that she buys hers from the dollar store. I laughed, because she’s forever complaining about the wrap she uses, and she’s definitely not paying less in the long run. I’ll address some of her many complains on her brand below. But here’s what I love about this wrap. The box: The lid makes this easy to pull out. I never have to find a torn end that’s disappeared into the roll. But also, there is a child safe blade on these. When you open the box, you pull the plastic box strip from the center and slide it onto the box. The blade is attached on that strip and just slides back and forth for ease of use. Also, the box is not much bigger than your average dollar store box so this fits nicely under my counter. Because the box weights more, and is better made, it never tears and I can wrap things without ever having to pick up the box. Just pull the wrap right over the dish, slide the blade, and go. One 750 ft roll of Kirkland lasts me nearly a year; I ordered my last 2-pack in March 2022 and ran out in early January of 2024. Here are some issues she has with dollar tree wrap: *The role is WAY smaller, so she buys it way more often. *She has scratched herself on the lame blade that’s attached to the box. *Not only a small roll, but she has to use a LOT MORE product. *She is always complaining about how frustrating it is to use her wrap, it will tear or get tangled, then she has to find the beginning and wastes product every time this happens, *She often has to use a second layer due to holes, or to make it more sturdy for travel or for meat and often goes all the way around the dish because she can’t get a seal. *It doesn’t work well in the micro, melts easily. *Can be tricky to get the right suction on the thing you’re covering. *It’s easy to accidentally poke holes into it while trying to wrap stuff. *The last bit of ANY wrap left on the role of any brand is always a little wonky, so the more often you’re replacing the roll, the more often you’re wasting that last bit of product from the end of the roll. There is a saying, “Penny wise, pound foolish.” It means you are paying less for something in the moment but spending WAY more for the item then you needed to if you’d spent a little more for a better version. TIP TO REHEAT RICE This wrap is perfect for reheating rice from the refrigerator but I also FREEZE leftover rice, then just thaw it and use this method. Easy…once you use this a couple times, you never need directions again. 1. Put rice in a GLASS bowl. 2. Add just a teaspoon of water. 3. Cover so edges of bowl are sealed. 4. Microwave until the wrap forms that stretchy bubble top from the steam and the bottom of the bowl is hot. For me that’s 1 1/2 to 2 minutes. 5. Let set for 5 minutes or so, don’t touch the cover. It set for 10-15 minutes. 6. Carefully remove the wrap. Your rice will look terrible, all smashed down. 7. JUST STIR IT, preferably with a fork, and it’s as good as fresh made. The water and steam reconstitute that little bit of dryness that happens.
